tools.name: get_user_account
tools.description: Get the Pinterest account behind this token: username, account type, and board, pin, follower and monthly-view counts

ad_account_id.description: Optional ad account ID whose owner becomes the operation user_account (Business Access)

tools.name: list_boards
tools.description: List the Pinterest boards owned by this account plus group boards it collaborates on, newest first

bookmark.description: Optional cursor from a previous response, to fetch the next page

privacy.description: Optional privacy filter (default returns every board the token's scopes allow)

ad_account_id.description: Optional ad account ID whose owner becomes the operation user_account (Business Access)

tools.name: list_pins
tools.description: List the Pins owned by this Pinterest account across all of its boards

bookmark.description: Optional cursor from a previous response, to fetch the next page

pin_filter.description: Optional filter to apply to the Pins

include_protected_pins.description: Whether to include protected Pins (default false)

domain.description: Optional exact link domain to filter by, with no 'www.' prefix (e.g. quox.ai)

tools.name: get_board
tools.description: Get one Pinterest board by ID, including its Pin, follower and collaborator counts

tools.name: list_board_pins
tools.description: List the Pins on one Pinterest board owned by or shared with this account

bookmark.description: Optional cursor from a previous response, to fetch the next page

needs_review: auth left as scaffolded (bearer on access_token) because the v5 reference confirms it: every operation's security block is pinterest_oauth2 / client_credentials, and Pinterest's own generated code sample for GET /v5/user_account sets the header verbatim 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>'. The pinterest vault type collects exactly one field, access_token, which is the wire shape this API wants.

NOT blind-provable beyond the auth wall, and a lifecycle caveat the vault cannot express: Pinterest access tokens are OAuth-issued and expire, so a pasted token works until it does not. Promoting this connector to oauth2_refresh would need client_id, client_secret and refresh_token fields added to the pinterest vault type first. The WIRE format is right either way, so the spec stays bearer.

category set to media (was uncategorized). Pinterest is a content/social surface, which is where twitch, spotify, canva and unsplash already sit; the wave's allowed list has no 'social' or plain 'marketing' value.

tools_source is the v5 reference itself. Every path, parameter, enum and response field below was read from the OpenAPI document embedded in developers.pinterest.com/docs/api/v5/ (operations user_account/get, boards/list, pins/list, boards/get, boards/list_pins), not from memory.

page_size clamps to default 25 / max 250 on all three list tools, verbatim from the reference: page_size schema is {"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":250,"default":25}. Pagination is bookmark-cursor based, so bookmark is a passthrough input rather than an offset.

board_id carries a _probe hint of 549755885175, which is Pinterest's own public example board ID from the boards/get response schema. Its board_id parameter schema is pattern ^\d+$, so the harness's generic 'quoxprobe' input could only ever produce a validation error; a well-formed but nonexistent numeric ID exercises the real route. It is a documentation value, never a credential.

list_pins omits the documented creative_types and domains parameters: both are array-valued and joined comma-separated on the wire, which this spec's query templating does not express. The scalar domain filter is included instead.

Shape-proof outcome: SHAPE_PROVEN, 6 of 6 probes. The bogus control path on api.pinterest.com answers 404 while every declared path answers 401 application/json with a dummy bearer, so the differential proves host, TLS, base_url, the Authorization header name and all five routes. Only the credential is missing; the token lifecycle caveat above is still not proven by this run.

No analytics tools here. GET /v5/user_account/analytics and the per-pin analytics operations all require start_date/end_date plus metric_types, and the reference notes known performance issues on the filtered pin paths, so they are left for a later pass rather than half-declared.
